item.title: Meta Launches Muse AI Assistant for Productivity and Personal Tasks
item.description:
Meta Launches Muse AI Assistant for Productivity and Personal Tasks

Meta has launched Muse, its first foray into AI-powered productivity tools. The company describes the AI agent as a tool designed to “take the busywork off your plate” by assisting with tasks such as emails, trip-planning, and online shopping.

🧩 How it works

Muse operates using a cloud-based virtual computer to carry out actions. To function, the agent requires permissions to access third-party accounts; for example, connecting to a Google account allows Muse to access, read, and delete emails.

⚙️ Key details

Muse includes a variety of generative and organizational capabilities:

  • Content Generation: Creates images, videos, AI podcasts, and interactive documents or webpages called “artifacts”.
  • Information Retrieval: A “Feed” tab that generates news summaries based on text prompts.
  • Organization: Maintains a running list of “goals” to complete and a list of personalized “ideas” for tool usage.
  • Personalization: Can provide side-by-side product comparisons and track Pokémon card releases.
Feature Capability
Online Shopping Can pick out and purchase items based on size, style, and color
Email Management Can delete promotional emails and updates
Subscriptions Can find and cancel forgotten subscriptions

💡 Why it matters

Tests of the tool reveal varying results regarding safety and data access. Muse refused to generate images of an “Apple CEO” or specific cartoon characters, yet it successfully generated images and video of a product launch event featuring Apple’s logo and device hallucinations.

Regarding privacy, Meta states it does not share information with advertisers and only exchanges data with third-party apps that is “needed for them to work for you.” However, Muse demonstrated the ability to access API data from connected Instagram and Facebook accounts to surface specific user interests not visible in the app’s UI, and it identified a user’s current location using a shipping address from an Amazon order.

#Meta #Muse #AIagents #Productivity

Source: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out

item.title: Meta Introduces Muse Personal AI Agent for Everyday Tasks
item.description:
Meta Introduces Muse Personal AI Agent for Everyday Tasks

Meta has launched Muse, a personal AI agent powered by the in-house Muse Spark model. The product is part of a multi-billion dollar strategy overhaul intended to revitalize Meta’s position in the AI race and catch up to rivals such as Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

🔍 Overview

Muse is described by Meta as a “personal AI agent” designed to put AI in the hands of virtually anyone. While Meta pitches it as “the world’s first personal AI agent built for everyone,” it is similar to various AI assistants and teammates offered by competitors.

🧩 How it works

Muse is designed to handle everyday tasks and projects. Its capabilities include:

  • Autonomous Action: Once given a goal, Muse can open a browser, fill out forms, and negotiate on behalf of users.
  • Background Processing: For lengthy tasks, Muse continues working after the app is closed and returns to the user if it requires approval (such as for a purchase) or if something changes.
  • Contextual Memory: The agent remembers details shared by users, even if mentioned only once, to provide unprompted suggestions.
  • Simple Interface: Users can communicate with the assistant via the Muse app or WhatsApp.

⚙️ Key details

Meta has focused on ease of use and privacy to distinguish Muse from other tools, many of which target technically-minded individuals or businesses.

Competitor Tool Target Audience/Nature
OpenAI ChatGPT Work Businesses or technically-minded individuals
Anthropic Claude Cowork Businesses or technically-minded individuals
Microsoft Copilot Tasks Businesses or technically-minded individuals
SpaceXAI Grok Bot Businesses or technically-minded individuals
Moltbot Viral open-source agent
Google Gemini Spark Similar audience to Muse

Privacy and Security:

  • Data Control: Users can opt out of their interactions being used to train Meta’s AI models and can instruct Muse to “forget” specific learned information.
  • Virtual Isolation: Muse runs on a virtual computer in the cloud to keep data separate from other agents.
  • Sentinel: A separate AI agent named Sentinel patrols the virtual machine to ensure Muse cannot reach the internet without approval.
  • Payment Security: Muse has no visibility into payment method passwords and currently supports secure checkout via Stripe’s Link, with 1Password and Shop Pay support coming soon.
  • Future Encryption: Meta plans to introduce a “confidential” version of the virtual machine later this year that is encrypted so even Meta cannot access it.

🚀 Availability

Muse will roll out in the US across the following platforms:

  • iOS
  • Android
  • muse.ai
  • AI glasses (coming soon)

The assistant will be free for most users, although Meta stated there will be paid subscriptions “for people who want to do more,” though costs and specific limits were not outlined.

#Meta #Muse #AIAgents #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
